question: A network engineer repeatedly saves a configuration on Catalyst switches to NVRAM using the write memory command. Which action should be taken to implement the same action on Nexus switches?
options: Use the alias command to use the write memory command.
Use the wri command to use the copy running-config startup-config command.
Use the exit command to leave the configuration mode and save the configuration automatically.
Use the write memory command to save the configuration.
theory: NX-OS does not natively support the classic IOS "write memory" shortcut for saving configuration (its native equivalent is "copy running-config startup-config"). To preserve familiar muscle memory from IOS-based Catalyst switches, an administrator can define a custom command alias on NX-OS that maps the text "write memory" (or a similar string) to execute "copy running-config startup-config" under the hood, rather than typing the native command every time. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — NX-OS Configuration Management)
